entries.text: Jordan River. A photo of a man in a long robe and head cloth standing on the bank of a calm green river, with trees and tall reeds along its banks. In verses 5 and 9, John baptizes people in the Jordan River, and Jesus is baptized there.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Sandals. A young man in a plain belted tunic and head cloth stands under a shade roof, holding a wooden staff, with sandals on his feet. In verse 7, John says he is not worthy to untie the sandals of the one who comes after him.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Sandals. A close view of feet in leather sandals on dusty ground: a wide strap over the toes and a strap around the ankle, fastened with a buckle. Straps like these are what John says, in verse 7, he is not worthy to stoop down and untie.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Wilderness or Desert. A view over dry, bare hills cut by deep gullies, with only scattered small bushes. Two people stand small at the bottom of the picture. In verse 4, John preaches in the wilderness; in verses 12 and 13, the Spirit drives Jesus into the wilderness for forty days.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Aerial View of Judea and Jerusalem. An illustrated view of the land from above, looking north. The Dead Sea is in front. The Jordan River flows into it from the Sea of Galilee far away. Jerusalem sits on the high hills of Judea, to the left. In verse 5, people go out from Jerusalem and the Judean countryside, down from these hills to the Jordan River, to be baptized.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Important Locations in Jerusalem. A close map of the city, with north at the top. A heavy black line marks the city walls, with the Temple and its outer courtyard on the east side. East, across the Kidron River, are the Mount of Olives and the road to Bethany. Mark 1 names Jerusalem only as a place people came from, in verse 5. The places marked here belong to later chapters of Mark.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Locations in the Book of Mark. A map with north at the top and the Mediterranean Sea on the left. The Jordan River runs south from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea. Galilee and Nazareth are in the north; Judea and Jerusalem are in the south. In this passage, people come from Jerusalem and Judea to the Jordan River, and Jesus comes from Nazareth in Galilee to be baptized there.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced

entries.text: Nazareth and Judea. A map with north at the top. A black arrow, marked in the key as travels of Jesus, runs from Nazareth in Galilee south down the Jordan valley to the river, north of the Dead Sea. A short arrow then points west, into Judea. In verse 9, Jesus comes from Nazareth in Galilee and is baptized by John in the Jordan. Follow the long arrow to trace that journey.
entries.borrow: bent (V1-4): shared base + Mark 1:1-13 line; PoC text replaced
